  "rationale": "Data: 6,766 works, each with exactly one passage (n_passages=1), so each work's rate is 0 or 1. Overall DISTANCE_TRAVEL rate is 0.107. All works have a year. Cutoff 1876: 752 works are early and 6,014 late. Estimand: in each of the 8 genres, take the mean rate of late works minus the mean rate of early works, then average the 8 differences equally. Result: -0.0258, 95% CI [-0.0516, -0.0001]. The CI is a normal approximation from binomial variances within each genre-period cell. It only just excludes zero. Direction by genre: falls in adventure, historical, collection, juvenile and romance; rises slightly in domestic_realist and sensation_mystery; flat in other. Artifact checks: (1) Author productivity differs sharply. Early works' authors average 9.6 works in the corpus versus 22.4 for late works. (2) Genre mix shifts somewhat: juvenile rises from 29% to 33%. Origin and n_editions are balanced. (3) Date confidence: 'high' falls from 49% to 46% of works and 'low' rises from 23% to 28%. Stratifying by date confidence changes the result: high -0.044 (CI [-0.083, -0.006]), medium -0.023, low +0.012, so the sign flips. (4) An OLS model adjusting for genre, origin, date_confidence, log n_editions and log author productivity, with standard errors clustered by author, gives -0.025 with CI [-0.050, 0.001], which includes zero. (5) Restricting to a narrower window (1856-1895) gives -0.013 with CI [-0.049, 0.024]. (6) Decade rates do not move steadily in one direction: about 0.12-0.15 in 1830-1880, a dip to 0.083 in the 1890s, then 0.10-0.11 after 1900. So the contrast depends heavily on the 1890s dip and on when the window starts. Restricting to well-dated works or to low-productivity authors makes the decrease larger, which is some support for a real decline. But the main CI only barely excludes zero, the adjusted and clustered CI includes zero, the narrow-window estimate is null, and the low-confidence stratum reverses. Alternative explanations: the corpus samples prolific late authors more heavily; the early sample is small and may lean toward travel-heavy adventure and historical works; a dip specific to the 1890s; and noise in dating. The cited passages are well-dated works coded for travel. They show the construct but cannot establish a trend. The evidence suggests a weak decrease but does not meet the bar for a robust historical shift, so I abstain."
